title: Retrograde global surfaces of section in the planar circular restricted three-body problem
statement: For every mass ratio $0<\mu<1$ and Hamiltonian energy below the first Lagrange critical value in the planar circular restricted three-body problem, prove that a geometric retrograde periodic orbit around a labelled primary bounds a rational disk-like global surface of section in the corresponding collision-regularized bounded component. On the Levi-Civita double cover, require an embedded disk bounded by the closed double lift of that orbit, with interior transverse to the flow and every nonbinding trajectory returning in both time directions.
assumptions: Use the planar Newtonian circular restricted problem with primary masses 1-mu and mu, and an energy strictly below H_mu(L1); fix the bounded component around one labelled primary.
Regularize collision with the labelled primary and use the complete regularized Hamiltonian flow compatible with the antipodal quotient.
The prime retrograde orbit is a collision-free, reflection-symmetric simple physical loop of winding +1 around that primary; this does not impose pointwise monotonic angular motion.
The disk boundary covers the prime quotient orbit twice, its quotient interior is embedded, and every trajectory outside the binding meets the page at arbitrarily large positive and negative times.
The target asserts existence of a suitable retrograde binding and one global page, not that every retrograde orbit works, not a full open-book fibration, and not integrability of the three-body flow.
physics_motivation: A global section converts regularized celestial-mechanics motion into a two-dimensional return map, making periodic orbits and recurrence accessible across the full subcritical parameter range.
resolution_target: A global-section existence theorem for all stated mass ratios and subcritical energies, or a counterexample satisfying the same geometric and return conditions.
status_note: The inspected Prove2Me mission has an open headline goal. Liu and Salomao's May 2026 revision proves the retrograde-section result near equal masses at all subcritical energies; their June 2026 Hill theorem concerns a limiting model. Narrow validated parameter ranges and existence of retrograde orbits do not settle the universal finite-mass global-section assertion. This is distinct from Birkhoff's conjecture about integrable billiard tables. The mission statement and cited recent abstracts were checked, not independently proof-audited or exhaustively traced through later literature.

title: Thomson problem for nine charges: global optimality of a tricapped trigonal prism
statement: For nine distinct points on the unit sphere, with Coulomb energy $E_N(x)=\sum_{i<j}\|x_i-x_j\|^{-1}$, prove that some member of the one-parameter tricapped trigonal-prism family is a global minimizer over all nine-point configurations. The family has two aligned equilateral triangles at heights $+h$ and $-h$, scaled to lie on the sphere, and three equatorial caps in the directions of the rectangular-face centers, with $0<h<1$.
assumptions: Fix N=9, unit sphere in R^3, distinct points, and the pair potential 1/r; these are equal classical point charges with no additional interactions.
The two latitude triangles have azimuths 2*pi*k/3, k=0,1,2, and the equatorial caps have azimuths pi/3+2*pi*k/3. The latitude radius is sqrt(1-h^2).
The latitude h is existentially quantified and must be certified or optimized rigorously; no guessed decimal or closed-form height is prescribed.
Competing configurations are arbitrary, with no prism, reflection or rotational symmetry assumption. A global minimizer need not be unique.
physics_motivation: Nine repelling charges on a spherical shell provide a small, physically defined energy landscape where numerical candidates must be distinguished from globally certified ground states.
resolution_target: A rigorous global lower bound attained by a member of the stated family, possibly computer-assisted, or a certified configuration below the rigorously minimized energy of every family member.
status_note: The inspected Prove2Me mission lists N=9 as an unresolved family-optimality target; its headline N=32 goal does not resolve this case. Finding a stationary family member, verifying a local minimum, or comparing only symmetric competitors does not establish global optimality. Known smaller-N results are background. This record preserves the source's provisional status; no full current-literature or optimality-proof audit was performed.

title: Thomson problem for ten charges: global optimality of a capped square antiprism
statement: For ten distinct points on the unit sphere with Coulomb energy $E_N(x)=\sum_{i<j}\|x_i-x_j\|^{-1}$, prove that some member of the one-parameter capped square-antiprism family globally minimizes the energy over all ten-point configurations. The candidate consists of the north and south poles and square latitude rings at heights $+h$ and $-h$, with a relative azimuthal offset $\pi/4$ and $0<h<1$.
assumptions: Fix N=10, unit sphere in R^3, distinct equal charges, and the unmodified Coulomb pair potential 1/r.
Each ring has radius sqrt(1-h^2); the upper azimuths are k*pi/2 and the lower azimuths are pi/4+k*pi/2, k=0,1,2,3.
The optimal latitude is not prescribed numerically: the claim is existence of a globally optimal member of the family.
Competitors need not contain antipodal points or have any symmetry. Local stability, family-restricted minimization and uniqueness are different assertions.
physics_motivation: The ten-charge sphere problem tests whether a numerically favorable, highly symmetric electrostatic arrangement is the true unrestricted ground state.
resolution_target: A global energy certificate attained at some admissible latitude, or a rigorously lower-energy counterexample to every member of the candidate family.
status_note: The Prove2Me description selects N=10 as a proposed early target because its antipodal poles may simplify proof cases. This is a project-selection observation, not a proof or an allowed restriction on competing configurations. The N=9 and N=32 targets have separate mathematical content. Source scope was checked; the full literature and any proof have not been independently audited.

title: Thomson problem for 32 charges: global optimality of the icosahedron-dodecahedron configuration
aliases: Icosahedron plus dual dodecahedron Coulomb optimality
statement: Let $X_{32}$ contain the 12 vertices of a regular icosahedron centered at the origin and the 20 directions through its face centers, all normalized to the unit sphere. Prove that $E_N(X_{32})\le E_N(Y)$ for every configuration $Y$ of 32 distinct points on the unit sphere, where $E_N(x)=\sum_{i<j}\|x_i-x_j\|^{-1}$. Equivalently, certify global Coulomb optimality of the icosahedron together with its dual dodecahedron.
assumptions: Use equal classical charges on the same unit sphere and the potential 1/r; the two polyhedra do not occupy shells of different radius.
Fix the relative orientation by the icosahedron/face-center duality; independent rotation of the dodecahedron defines a different configuration.
All 32-point competitors are allowed, without symmetry or polyhedral restrictions. The conjecture does not require uniqueness up to rotation.
physics_motivation: A 32-charge electrostatic ground state is a stringent test of global energy bounds beyond smaller spherical configurations with established exact certificates.
resolution_target: An unrestricted global-optimality proof for the stated exact configuration, or a rigorously lower-energy 32-point configuration.
status_note: This is the inspected Prove2Me mission's open headline goal, ThomsonCampaign.thomson_thirty_two. The source presents the polyhedral configuration as numerically best known; neither that numerical comparison nor a finite-precision local optimization proves this universal inequality. Source statement and scope were checked without an independent proof audit or exhaustive status review.

title: KPZ variance scaling for one-dimensional ballistic deposition
aliases: Ballistic deposition height fluctuations of order t^(1/3)
statement: Consider continuous-time nearest-neighbor ballistic deposition on $\mathbb Z$, started from the flat profile $\xi_0(x)=0$, with independent rate-one Poisson clocks at each column. When the clock at $x$ rings, set $\xi_t(x)=\max\{\xi_{t-}(x)+1,\xi_{t-}(x-1),\xi_{t-}(x+1)\}$ and leave other columns unchanged. Prove that constants $0<c\le C<\infty$ and $T<\infty$ exist such that $c t^{2/3}\le\operatorname{Var}(\xi_t(0))\le C t^{2/3}$ for every $t\ge T$.
assumptions: Use the infinite one-dimensional substrate, nearest-neighbor sticking rule, unit block height, flat initial condition and independent rate-one clocks specified in the statement.
Define the infinite process through its standard graphical construction or a justified limit of finite boxes; do not replace it by independent random deposition.
Constants may depend on this fixed model but not on time. Variance is the centered second moment and must be finite.
The target is a two-sided variance exponent. Convergence to a Tracy-Widom distribution, a precise leading amplitude and general KPZ universality are stronger, separate statements.
physics_motivation: Ballistic deposition is a concrete growth model without known exact solvability, so its predicted fluctuations test KPZ universality beyond integrable models.
resolution_target: Matching positive upper and lower bounds of order t^(2/3) for the variance at all sufficiently large times, or a rigorous incompatible asymptotic law for this same model.
status_note: The inspected Prove2Me headline goal remains open. Its bibliography identifies Penrose's logarithmic lower bound, while Sudijono's September 2026 abstract proves a linear upper bound in time; neither gives the predicted t^(2/3) law. The mission's current goal is the variance exponent, not its stronger unformalized Tracy-Widom prediction. This differs from our quantum Heisenberg-chain KPZ target and our KPZ problems in two or more spatial dimensions. Source formulation and the recent upper-bound abstract were checked; no exhaustive literature or proof audit was performed.
